reason: This is a compensation/feedforward capacitor from an internal node to the output; removing it typically doesn’t prevent DC operation or basic differential amplification. It mainly affects frequency response (stability/peaking, bandwidth) and transient behavior.
impact_estimate: Low for DC/functional behavior; moderate-to-high risk for AC stability and settling depending on load and bias conditions.

reason: Like C1, this capacitor provides frequency shaping between an internal node and the output and is not required for the amplifier’s core biasing or DC gain mechanism. Deleting it usually preserves basic operation but changes high-frequency dynamics and may reduce phase margin.
impact_estimate: Low for DC/functional behavior; moderate-to-high risk for AC response symmetry and stability.

reason: This is a diode-connected PMOS tied to node net70; in many differential amplifier topologies, net70 is already defined/held by other devices (e.g., the NMOS network M10/M14 and PMOS M1), so this device often just adds extra bias clamping or start-up help. If net70 has a valid DC path and doesn’t need a clamp to VDD, removing M6 typically has minimal effect.
impact_estimate: Usually low if net70 remains properly biased; can be high if net70 otherwise floats at startup or if M6 is needed to establish the intended common-mode/bias point.
